subject: Is there a way to read newick files directly

messages.author: 4de26959f6d811fb
messages.subject: Is there a way to read newick files directly
parts:
Hello,


I tried to read newick files, but it returns the following error.

tree <- read.tree("file.nwk")            tree <- read.newick("file.nwk")

Error in FUN(X[[i]], ...) : attempt to set index 19/19 in SET_STRING_ELT


However, when I read it as text it works fine 

tree <- "(((H197:0.0572,(((H240:6E-05,(H198:0.18615,(H228:6E-05,(H199:6E-05,H220:0)I1:0)I2:0)I3:0)I4:0.00268,H206:0.00269)I5:0.01014,(H225:0.00268,(H265:0,H230:0)I6:0)I7:0.00895)I8:0.03254)I9:0.09191)A:0);"

T <- read.tree(text = tree)


Is there a way to read newick files directly ? (Instead of copying and pasting it as text and then reading it as newick file?)


I tried using phytools but it introduces NAs. [In getEdgeLength: NAs introduced by coercion ----> The resulting tree has 0 edge lengths]



Thank you,
SDU

messages.author: 1d63b70cc6085e65
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to read newick files directly
parts:
But the branch support values are bb/alrt and can’t be parsed by the standard newick reader.  So you can either replace the “/“ with “_” or read it in as iqtree format.  

Sent from my iPhone

On 4 Apr 2019, at 12:30, Chad Fibke <fi...@ualberta.ca> wrote:


You can also replace the .nwk extension to a .tree. Then you can use read.tree(file.tree)! 

On Wed, Apr 3, 2019 at 6:13 PM Mark Schultz <dr.mark...@gmail.com> wrote:
You need to do read.iqtree
